normalized.description: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. It acknowledges that University College Cork contracted with Collecte Localisation Satellites (CLS), for the provision of support of online learning resource development and enhancement, training expertise and scientific oversight for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service, under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. CLS will (i) support the online learning resource activities for the overall Service contract, providing technical support to implement resource solutions, (ii) contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee, and (iii) support Training event implementation. CLS were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They have extensive experience in developing integrated offers to a broad range of Service-relevant stakeholders including: government, industry and the scientific community and services, in sectors such as Environment & climate monitoring, Mobility, Energy & infrastructures, amongst others. They have a dedicated team of data scientists who work closely with oceanographers to develop new methodologies, understandings and ocean science communications. They have coupled this with a growing, and impressive training portfolio in Earth Observation applications - critical to the Copernicus programme – and are existing suppliers of data and training materials to the Copernicus Climate Service, and Copernicus Marine Service (in addition to ESA, CNES and many other global partners, which brought considerable potential for synergies to the Service). CLS have also delivered staff training programmes to field and IT operators and end-users, while having also developed a full Moodle course for EUMETSAT, and a range of Jupyter applications and notebooks, the bedrock of the ECMWF's online training offering. Their staff are experienced in delivering in-person training on ocean scient topics such as altimetry, a key area for capacity building in the Copernicus community. In addition, they bring their oceans experience, training experience and knowledge of satellite systems to satisfy a critical niche for expertise in the Service’s Scientific Advisory Committee - a key Quality Control mechanism embedded within the contract Service. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The company was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.
